newsitem.title: UK: Dorling sees shake-out in U.S.multimedia mkt.
newsitem.headline: Dorling sees shake-out in U.S.multimedia mkt.

text.p: British publisher Dorling Kindersley said on Monday that oversupply was creating tough conditions in the U.S. retail market for multimedia products.
"Multimedia, particularly in the U.S., is very tough this year and we recognise that," chairman and chief executive Peter Kindersley told a press conference.
"People have become too competitive, they are trying to create a mass market for something which is not a mass market product," he added.
But he added that a stable market for CD-ROMs should emerge once the shake-up in the U.S. was complete.
The multimedia division had a turnover of 21.2 million stg in 1996, 47 percent of which was generated in the U.S.
Multimedia turnover was up by over 60 percent and Dorling Kindersley executives said that it should continue to grow in the current year despite the tough U.S. retail market.
"In the UK, multimedia is strong and it is holding up well in the rest of the world," said Kindersley, adding that "competition to the edge of the precipice" existed only in the U.S. retail market.
Alan Buckingham, managing director of Dorling Kindersley multimedia, said that latest figures showed that 55 million homes worldwide have multimedia PCs.
He forecast that would rise to 75 million by the end of next year and called it a "huge potential market".
He said that five of the company's titles released this autumn would be "hybrid" CD-ROMs, which allow online access.
However, he said it was not yet clear whether online publishing would prove profitable. Things would become clearer once the "swirling dust storm of hype" cleared, he added.
